subject: Civil Engineering
title: Shallow Foundations: Footings and Mats
description: One-minute skill: Shallow Foundations: Footings and Mats.

hook.text: Most houses rest on simple concrete pads a few feet underground. That's a footing.

buildup.text: Spread footings widen the load over a larger area — like snowshoes on soft snow.

discovery.text: Mat foundations are one giant slab under the entire building — load spread evenly.

twist.text: Shallow foundations only work when strong soil lies near the surface.

climax.text: The Burj Khalifa's mat foundation is 12 feet thick and covers half an acre.

punchline.text: Spread the load wide enough and even soft soil cooperates.

quiz.question: How does a spread footing reduce pressure on the soil?
options: It pushes the load sideways instead of downward
It distributes the load over a wider area, reducing pressure per unit
It transfers load directly to bedrock through steel rods

details.summary: Shallow foundations transfer structural loads near the ground surface through footings or mat foundations. Isolated footings support individual columns, strip footings support walls, combined footings support two or more columns.
details.whyItMatters: Shallow foundations are the most common and economical foundation type, suitable when competent soil exists near the surface. They support the majority of low to mid-rise buildings worldwide.
takeaways: Isolated footings are the simplest and most economical for adequate soil conditions
Mat foundations spread load over the entire building footprint for weak soils
Footing design must satisfy both bearing capacity and settlement requirements

faq.question: How deep should a shallow foundation be placed?
faq.answer: Minimum depth is typically 0.5 to 1.5 meters to reach below topsoil, frost depth, and the zone of seasonal moisture change. Deeper placement increases bearing capacity but costs more for excavation.

faq.question: When is a mat foundation preferred over individual footings?
faq.answer: Mat foundations are used when individual footings would be so large they nearly overlap, when soil is very weak and loads must be spread over maximum area, when differential settlement must be minimized, or when hydrostatic uplift requires the building's full weight to resist floating.
